about.title: Calipatria Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Calipatria is small enough that a sudden death is felt across the whole community, not just one household. Fewer than 7,500 people live here, and grief in a town this size rarely stays private. If a spouse, parent, or child was taken by someone else's negligence, California law gives certain family members the right to bring a civil wrongful death action. That claim runs separately from any criminal case, and it can move forward whether or not charges are ever filed. Public collision records for Calipatria are quiet: the most recent final year lists no traffic deaths, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday mornings along Access Road and Blair Road. Yet wrongful death is not only a roadway issue. Farm equipment, unsafe worksites, medical mistakes, and hazardous property all take lives in Imperial County. Standing is limited, and the filing window is generally two years from the date of death, shorter when a government agency is involved. We handle wrongful death claims directly. Our team can review what happened at no cost to you.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims against a public entity carry a much shorter clock. An early conversation protects your right to be heard.

items.title: Every Category of Loss Considered
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Calipatria's crash records show no traffic deaths recently. Can a wrongful death claim still apply here?
items.answer: Yes. Roadway fatalities are only one source of wrongful death claims, and public collision counts do not capture deaths from farm or workplace accidents, medical negligence, or unsafe property. If someone's carelessness contributed to the loss of your family member in Calipatria, our team can evaluate whether a civil claim is available regardless of how the death is categorized in traffic data.

items.question: Does a wrongful death case depend on a criminal conviction?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, entirely separate from any prosecution by the Imperial County District Attorney. It can proceed even if no charges are filed or a criminal case ends without a conviction, because the civil standard of proof is different.

items.question: What if a county or state vehicle was involved in my loved one's death?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a shorter, separate process with an early notice requirement, well before the standard two-year deadline. Missing that window can end the claim before it starts. Because of this, it is wise to speak with an attorney as soon as you are able, and we can discuss your case at no cost.
